definition: In natural language processing, language identification or language guessing is the problem of determining which natural language a given content is in.
details: Computational approaches to this problem view it as a special case of text categorization, solved with various statistical methods.

explainer.lead: Language identification is the problem of determining which natural language a given content is in. It matters as a prerequisite step for routing and processing multilingual text.

tiers.eli5: It's how a system looks at a piece of text and figures out, say, that it's Portuguese and not Spanish.
tiers.practitioner: Computational approaches treat it as a special case of text categorization and solve it with statistical methods. The pitfall is short or mixed-language content, where there is too little signal to categorize reliably.
tiers.paperLevel: In NLP, language identification (or language guessing) is the problem of determining which natural language a given content is in; computationally it is viewed as a special case of text categorization, solved with various statistical methods.

explainer.example: An incoming support message is classified as French before being routed to a French-language model.
